This PR implements the foundational RSMD PR0 milestone, establishing pulldown-cmark as the core HTML renderer while introducing basic WASM bindings for JavaScript integration.

### Key Changes

#### Core Implementation

- clarifying that HTML now fully delegates to pulldown-cmark while headings remain a temporary line-scan pass
- keep the render() API surface unchanged but expand surrounding docs to highlight the two-pass trade-off
- add comprehensive documentation explaining current state: HTML accuracy prioritized, heading collection as best-effort
- normalize implementation to use pulldown-cmark for all CommonMark + GFM rendering

#### WASM Integration

- Introduce new WASM bindings module gated to wasm32 target
- export render_wasm() function with serde-powered option decoding for JS callers
- export slugify_wasm() function for standalone slug generation
- enable JavaScript callers to use the Rust renderer directly via wasm-bindgen

Extracts mock data generation from `ChatService` into a dedicated static class:

- `GenerateMockAdaptiveCard()` - Generates weather, status, profile, or default cards based on message keywords

// Before: Instance method in ChatService
private string GenerateMockResponse(string userMessage) { ... }

// After: Static method in dedicated provider
public static class MockDataProvider {
    public static string GenerateMockResponse(string userMessage) { ... }
    public static string GenerateMockAdaptiveCard(string userMessage) { ... }
}
```

### Summary
This PR fixes erratic bot painting behavior, optimizes performance and speed, and completely modernizes the main window user interface for GarticBot.

### Details
- Corrected rectangle and line calculation algorithms to ensure clean, accurate strokes and prevent random color fills or over-painting.
- Dramatically increased drawing speeds for all speed selections; delays now scale more naturally with segment length.
- Refactored color selection: more robust simulated input and channel focus; improved palette click timing.
- Rewrote the main window to use a clean, card-style layout with modern button and control styles (no more asset-reliant toggles).
- Improved resource management, cancellation handling, progress feedback, and input validation.
- Guarded operations against running without a loaded image, with clear error reporting.
- All updates are internal and UI/user-visible, requiring no migration by users except running on a Windows host for correct WPF operation.

## Summary

Adds complete Numerical Methods section documenting GANDALF's spectral implementation.

### Key Content

**Fourier Spectral Discretization**
- 3D Fourier representation with real FFT optimization
- Spectral derivatives (exact for smooth fields)
- Typical resolution: 128³ to 256³ capturing k⊥ρᵢ ~ 1

**GANDALF Integrating Factor Time Stepping**
- Removes stiff Alfvén wave CFL restriction via exp(±ikz·t) factors
- Second-order Runge-Kutta (midpoint method) for nonlinear terms
- O(dt²) temporal accuracy, exact linear propagation
- Adaptive CFL-based timestep selection

**Dissipation Treatment**
- Normalized hyper-resistivity: exp[-η(k⊥²/k²⊥,max)^r Δt]
- Normalized hyper-collisions: exp[-ν(m/M)^(2n) Δt]
- Resolution-independent overflow constraints

**Dealiasing**
- 2/3 rule for pseudospectral stability
- Critical for long-time turbulence simulations

**Convergence Properties**
- Spectral (exponential) spatial convergence
- Second-order temporal convergence
- Exponential velocity-space convergence via Hermite moments
- Energy conservation <0.01% error in inviscid case

**JAX Implementation**
- JIT compilation to optimized kernels
- Hardware portability (CPU/GPU/TPU/Metal)
- Functional design with pytree structures
- 70-90% of hand-optimized Fortran performance

### Includes

- 2 comprehensive algorithm boxes
- 14 numbered equations
- Graduate-level JPP-appropriate exposition
- Proper LaTeX compilation (algorithm/algorithmic packages added)

body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **4.5.3** to **7.11.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.11.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was
  claimed to come from a non-Python file, a ``NotPython`` exception could be
  raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to
  Python, as reported in `issue 2077`_. This is now fixed.

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

.. _issue 2077: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2077


.. _changes_7-11-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how
  conflicting settings are handled. The "sysmon" core cannot be used with some
  conurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with
  branch measurement.

  - If the core is not specified and defaults to "sysmon" (Python 3.14+), but
    other settings conflict with sysmon, then the "ctrace" core will be used
    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: if the measurement core defaults to "sysmon" (the default for Python
  3.14+ since v7.9.1), but sysmon can't support some aspect of your
  configuration (concurrency settings, dynamic contexts, and so on), then the
  ctrace core is used instead. Previously, this would result in an error.
  An explicit request
  for sysmon with conflicting settings will still result in an error. Closes
  `issue 2064`_.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

.. _issue 1420: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1420
.. _issue 2064: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2064
.. _issue 2070: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2070


.. _changes_7-11-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.9, declared support for Python 3.15 alpha.


.. _changes_7-10-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.7
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Performance: with branch coverage in large files, generating HTML, JSON, or
  LCOV reports could take far too long due to some quadratic behavior when
  creating the function and class index pages.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2048`_.  Thanks to Daniel Diniz for help diagnosing the problem.

- Most warnings and a few errors now have links to a page in the docs
  explaining the specific message.  Closes `issue 1921`_.

.. _issue 1921: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1921
.. _issue 2048: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2048


.. _changes_7-10-6:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.6
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: ``source`` directories were not properly communicated to subprocesses
  that ran in different directories, as reported in `issue 1499`_.  This is now
  fixed.

- Performance: `Alex Gaynor continues fine-tuning <pull 2038_>`_ the speed of
  combination, especially with many contexts.

.. _issue 1499: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/1499
.. _pull 2038: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/pull/2038


.. _changes_7-10-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.5
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Big speed improvements for ``coverage combine``: it's now about twice as
  fast! Huge thanks to Alex Gaynor for pull requests `2032 <pull 2032_>`_,

author: gounthar
body:
## Summary
- Improves robustness of retry/recovery error handling in both APT and RPM workflows
- Addresses CodeRabbit feedback from PR #116
- Applies consistent patterns across both workflows

## Changes

### 1. Rebase Detection - Filesystem-Based (Both Workflows)

**Before:**
```bash
if git status | grep -q "rebase in progress"; then
  git rebase --abort
fi
```

**After:**
```bash
if [ -d .git/rebase-merge ] || [ -d .git/rebase-apply ]; then
  git rebase --abort
fi
```

**Why:**
- ✅ Git-version-independent (doesn't parse human-readable output)
- ✅ More robust across different git configurations
- ✅ Checks actual filesystem state, not output format
- **Locations**: APT:290, RPM:295

### 2. Git Diff Error Visibility (Both Workflows)

**Before:**
```bash
if ! git diff --quiet dists pool 2>/dev/null; then
```

**After:**
```bash
if ! git diff --quiet dists pool; then
```

**Why:**
- ✅ Surfaces real errors (permissions, missing paths) in workflow logs
- ✅ No silent error masking
- ✅ Better debugging when issues occur
- **Locations**: APT:316, RPM:342

### 3. GPG Key Re-import - Idempotent Check (RPM Workflow Only)

**Before:**
```bash
# Re-import GPG key (may have been cleared by reset)
echo "$GPG_PRIVATE_KEY" | gpg --batch --import 2>/dev/null || true
```

**After:**
```bash
# Re-import GPG key if needed (idempotent check)
if ! gpg --list-secret-keys 56188341425B007407229B48FB1963FC3575A39D &>/dev/null; then
  echo "Re-importing GPG signing key..."
  echo "$GPG_PRIVATE_KEY" | gpg --batch --import
else
  echo "GPG key already present, skipping re-import"
fi
```

**Why:**
- ✅ No `|| true` error masking (aligns with PR #116 goals)
- ✅ Idempotent - handles retry scenarios gracefully
- ✅ Clear logging of import vs skip decision
- ✅ Fails explicitly if import truly fails
- **Location**: RPM:318-323

**Note**: APT workflow doesn't use GPG in retry path, so no equivalent change needed.

## Benefits

| Benefit | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Consistency** | Same patterns applied to both APT and RPM workflows |
| **No Silent Failures** | All errors surface in logs with context |
| **Version Independence** | Filesystem checks don't depend on git output format |
| **Better Debugging** | Clear error messages and state indicators |
| **Idempotency** | Retry logic handles already-completed operations gracefully |

## Testing Strategy

- [x] Code review against issue requirements
- [x] Verified all changes align with CodeRabbit feedback
- [x] Confirmed consistency across both workflows
- [ ] Test with manual workflow dispatch
- [ ] Test with concurrent package builds (will happen naturally)
- [ ] Verify improved error messages in logs

## Rationale for Choices

### Why filesystem checks over `git status`?
Git's status output is designed for humans and can vary across versions, locales, and configurations. Checking `.git/rebase-merge` or `.git/rebase-apply` directly is the canonical way to detect rebase state.

### Why idempotent GPG check instead of `|| true`?
The `|| true` pattern masks **all** errors, including legitimate failures. The idempotent check:
- Succeeds when key is already present (expected in retries)
- Fails explicitly when import fails (unexpected, needs investigation)
- Provides clear logging for debugging

### Why remove `2>/dev/null` from git diff?
If `git diff` has stderr output, it usually indicates a real problem (permissions, corrupted repo, etc.) that should be visible in logs. Hiding it makes debugging harder.

## CodeRabbit Feedback Addressed

✅ **GPG Import Error Masking** - Replaced `|| true` with idempotent check  
✅ **Rebase Detection Fragility** - Using filesystem checks instead of output parsing  
✅ **Git Diff Stderr Redirect** - Removed to surface real errors

## Related

- Closes #117
- Follow-up to PR #116
- CodeRabbit review: https://github.com/gounthar/docker-for-riscv64/pull/116#pullrequestreview-3439751829

## Notes

These changes are pure improvements with no breaking changes. The workflows will continue to function exactly as before, but with better error handling and debugging capabilities.

author: rishiraj-58
body: ## Summary Fixes issue where expressions like `{{ 'https://' }}` inside JWT JSON payloads were incorrectly parsed, causing single quotes to be replaced with double quotes and breaking URLs. ### Root Cause The JWT node was using `parseJsonParameter` which has aggressive error recovery that replaces ALL single quotes with double quotes when JSON parsing fails. This caused expressions like `{{ 'https://' }}` to be evaluated and then incorrectly transformed to `"https"://`, creating invalid JSON. ### Changes Made 1. **Added preprocessing for raw expressions**: Similar to the Set node, the JWT node now detects when `claimsJson` starts with `=` and stores the raw expression for proper processing 2. **Added `resolveRawData` handling**: Expressions within the JSON string are now properly evaluated in context 3. **Use `jsonParse` directly**: For resolved expressions, we now use `jsonParse` directly instead of `parseJsonParameter` to avoid the aggressive error recovery 4. **Clean trailing commas**: Remove trailing commas before parsing (common in n8n workflows) ### Testing Steps 1. Import the workflow from issue #21658 2. Set up JWT credentials (passphrase-based for testing) 3. Execute the workflow 4. Verify the JWT token is generated successfully without the `"https"://` error ### Before { "aud": "https"://login.microsoftonline.com/tenant/oauth2/v2.0/token" }❌ Invalid JSON with broken URL ### After { "aud": "https://login.microsoftonline.com/tenant/oauth2/v2.0/token" }✅ Valid JSON with correct URL ## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts Fixes #21658 Related to #15773, #10972 ## Review / Merge checklist - [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md)) - [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created. - [ ] Tests included. - [ ] PR Labeled with `release/backport` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported) --- > [!NOTE] > No file changes are present in this diff. > > Written by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/dashboard?tab=bugbot) for commit 477ffea4ced772de7aa06033536c074a4720089a. author: copilot
body:
Program claimed to use BVCU voice files for synthesis but pyttsx3/eSpeak cannot read this proprietary Nuance format. User correctly identified the files were loaded but never actually used.

## Changes

- **Messaging**: Replace "✓ Using BVCU voice files" with "ℹ BVCU files detected (but not used - pyttsx3/eSpeak cannot read this format)"
- **Engine initialization**: Remove code that pretended to apply BVCU parameters (rate adjustment, dictionary enhancement)
- **Documentation**: Add explicit BVCU limitations section explaining format incompatibility
- **Comments**: Update docstrings to reflect detection-only behavior

## Before/After

**Before:**
```python
print("✓ Applying BVCU voice configuration to TTS engine")
print(f"✓ Voice rate adjusted based on BVCU data: {adjusted_rate}")
print("✓ Using BVCU voice files for enhanced synthesis")
```

**After:**
```python
print("ℹ Note: BVCU files detected but cannot be used by pyttsx3/eSpeak engine")
print("ℹ BVCU files require Nuance Vocalizer SDK (proprietary)")
print("ℹ BVCU files detected (but not used - pyttsx3/eSpeak cannot read this format)")
```

Files are still detected and loaded for compatibility but program now honestly communicates they have no effect on synthesis.

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) from **6.2.4** to **9.0.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 9.0.0
   ```
   =========================

New features
------------


- `1367 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1367>`_: **Support for subtests** has been added.

  :ref:`subtests <subtests>` are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time.

  Example:

  .. code-block:: python

      def contains_docstring(p: Path) -> bool:
          """Return True if the given Python file contains a top-level docstring."""
          ...


      def test_py_files_contain_docstring(subtests: pytest.Subtests) -> None:
          for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"):
              with subtests.test(path=str(path)):
                  assert contains_docstring(path)


  Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring.

  In addition, :meth:`unittest.TestCase.subTest` is now also supported.

  This feature was originally implemented as a separate plugin in `pytest-subtests <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-subtests>`__, but since then has been merged into the core.

  .. note::

      This feature is experimental and will likely evolve in future releases. By that we mean that we might change how subtests are reported on failure, but the functionality and how to use it are stable.


- `13743 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13743>`_: Added support for **native TOML configuration files**.

  While pytest, since version 6, supports configuration in ``pyproject.toml`` files under ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]``,
  it does so in an "INI compatibility mode", where all configuration values are treated as strings or list of strings.
  Now, pytest supports the native TOML data model.

  In ``pyproject.toml``, the native TOML configuration is under the ``[tool.pytest]`` table.

  .. code-block:: toml

       pyproject.toml
      [tool.pytest]
      minversion = "9.0"
      addopts = ["-ra", "-q"]
      testpaths = [
          "tests",
          "integration",
      ]

  The ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` table remains supported, but both tables cannot be used at the same time.

  If you prefer to use a separate configuration file, or don't use ``pyproject.toml``, you can use ``pytest.toml`` or ``.pytest.toml``:

  .. code-block:: toml

       pytest.toml or .pytest.toml
      [pytest]
      minversion = "9.0"
      addopts = ["-ra", "-q"]
      testpaths = [
          "tests",
          "integration",
      ]

  The documentation now (sometimes) shows configuration snippets in both TOML and INI formats, in a tabbed interface.

  See :ref:`config file formats` for full details.


- `13823 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13823>`_: Added a **"strict mode"** enabled by the :confval:`strict` configuration option.

  When set to ``true``, the :confval:`strict` option currently enables

  * :confval:`strict_config`
  * :confval:`strict_markers`
  * :confval:`strict_parametrization_ids`
  * :confval:`strict_xfail`

  The individual strictness options can be explicitly set to override the global :confval:`strict` setting.

  The previously-deprecated ``--strict`` command-line flag now enables strict mode.

  If pytest adds new strictness options in the future, they will also be enabled in strict mode.
  Therefore, you should only enable strict mode if you use a pinned/locked version of pytest,
  or if you want to proactively adopt new strictness options as they are added.

  See :ref:`strict mode` for more details.


- `13737 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13737>`_: Added the :confval:`strict_parametrization_ids` configuration option.

  When set, pytest emits an error if it detects non-unique parameter set IDs,
  rather than automatically making the IDs unique by adding `0`, `1`, ... to them.
  This can be particularly useful for catching unintended duplicates.


- `13072 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13072>`_: Added support for displaying test session **progress in the terminal tab** using the `OSC 9;4; <https://conemu.github.io/en/AnsiEscapeCodes.html#ConEmu_specific_OSC>`_ ANSI sequence.
  When pytest runs in a supported terminal emulator like ConEmu, Gnome Terminal, Ptyxis, Windows Terminal, Kitty or Ghostty,
  you'll see the progress in the terminal tab or window,
  allowing you to monitor pytest's progress at a glance.

  This feature is automatically enabled when running in a TTY. It is implemented as an internal plugin. If needed, it can be disabled as follows:
  - On a user level, using ``-p no:terminalprogress`` on the command line or via an environment variable ``PYTEST_ADDOPTS='-p no:terminalprogress'``.
  - On a project configuration level, using ``addopts = "-p no:terminalprogress"``.


- `478 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/478>`_: Support PEP420 (implicit namespace packages) as `--pyargs` target when :confval:`consider_namespace_packages` is `true` in the config.

  Previously, this option only impacted package imports, now it also impacts tests discovery.


- `13678 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13678>`_: Added a new :confval:`faulthandler_exit_on_timeout` configuration option set to "false" by default to let `faulthandler` interrupt the `pytest` process after a timeout in case of deadlock.

  Previously, a `faulthandler` timeout would only dump the traceback of all threads to stderr, but would not interrupt the `pytest` process.

  -- by :user:`ogrisel`.


- `13829 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13829>`_: Added support for configuration option aliases via the ``aliases`` parameter in :meth:`Parser.addini() <pytest.Parser.addini>`.

  Plugins can now register alternative names for configuration options,
  allowing for more flexibility in configuration naming and supporting backward compatibility when renaming options.
  The canonical name always takes precedence if both the canonical name and an alias are specified in the configuration file.



Improvements in existing functionality
--------------------------------------

- `13330 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13330>`_: Having pytest configuration spread over more than one file (for example having both a ``pytest.ini`` file and ``pyproject.toml`` with a ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` table) will now print a warning to make it clearer to the user that only one of them is actually used.

  -- by :user:`sgaist`


- `13574 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13574>`_: The single argument ``--version`` no longer loads the entire plugin infrastructure, making it faster and more reliable when displaying only the pytest version.

  Passing ``--version`` twice (e.g., ``pytest --version --version``) retains the original behavior, showing both the pytest version and plugin information.

  .. note::

      Since ``--version`` is now processed early, it only takes effect when passed directly via the command line. It will not work if set through other mechanisms, such as :envvar:`PYTEST_ADDOPTS` or :confval:`addopts`.


- `13823 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13823>`_: Added :confval:`strict_xfail` as an alias to the ``xfail_strict`` option,
  :confval:`strict_config` as an alias to the ``--strict-config`` flag,
  and :confval:`strict_markers` as an alias to the ``--strict-markers`` flag.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds API discovery and introspection capabilities to SmartSwitch:

- **`parent` parameter**: Organize multiple Switchers hierarchically within the same class
- **`entries()` method**: List all registered handler names for introspection
- **Comprehensive documentation**: New API Discovery guide with practical examples
- **Local CI configuration**: Add `.actrc` for local testing with act

## Features

### 1. Parent Parameter

Enables organizing multiple Switchers in the same class with a hierarchical structure:

```python
class MyAPI:
    # Main aggregator
    main = Switcher(name="main")
    
    # Logical groupings with parent reference
    users = Switcher(name="users", parent=main)
    posts = Switcher(name="posts", parent=main)
    
    @users
    def create_user(self, data):
        pass
    
    @posts
    def create_post(self, data):
        pass

# Navigate hierarchy
api = MyAPI()
assert api.users.parent is MyAPI.main
```

### 2. Entries Method

Introspect registered handlers at runtime:

```python
api = MyAPI()
print(api.users.entries())  # ['create_user']
print(api.posts.entries())  # ['create_post']
```

## Version Bump

- **Previous**: v0.2.2
- **New**: v0.3.0 (minor version bump for new features)

## Documentation

- New comprehensive guide: [docs/guide/api-discovery.md](docs/guide/api-discovery.md)
- Updated README with new features and examples
- Updated architecture diagrams with new methods and relationships

- ✅ All 62 tests passing

- ✅ Lint checks passed (ruff, black, mypy)

None - this is a backward compatible release.

body:
## Summary

This PR refocuses the package as a pure Node.js loader companion without public API exports, and adds comprehensive integration tests with real Node.js process execution.

### Key Changes

**1. Refocus as Loader Companion**
- Remove all public API exports (createResolver, TypeScriptResolver, type re-exports)
- Remove programmatic API documentation from README
- Update descriptions to clarify this is a companion to Node.js built-in TypeScript support
- Add `--experimental-transform-types` examples alongside Node.js 22 built-in type stripping
- Add directory imports feature to documentation
- Consolidate duplicate oxc-resolver mentions

**2. Integration Tests & Loader Fixes**
- Add 3 new integration test suites that spawn real Node.js processes:
  - Extensionless imports from TypeScript files
  - Directory imports (both index.ts and index.js)
  - File/directory priority resolution
- Add `initialize()` hook following the extensionless loader pattern
- Update `register()` call to pass `{ data: { argv, execArgv } }` argument
- Handle `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT` for proper directory import support
- Fix critical oxc-resolver bug: create new instances instead of using `cloneWithOptions()`
- Update `clearCache()` to clear all resolver instances
- Exclude test/fixtures from ESLint

### Root Cause

The oxc-resolver's `cloneWithOptions()` method was causing resolution failures when creating resolvers with conditions beyond `['node', 'import']`. The solution was to create new `ResolverFactory` instances with updated condition names instead of cloning.

### Test Results

✅ All 21 tests passing:
- 3 new integration tests (real Node.js process spawning)
- 18 existing unit tests (updated to work with new initialization)

  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.11.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was
  claimed to come from a non-Python file, a ``NotPython`` exception could be
  raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to
  Python, as reported in `issue 2077`_. This is now fixed.

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

.. _issue 2077: https://github.com/nedbat/coveragepy/issues/2077


.. _changes_7-11-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how
  conflicting settings are handled. The "sysmon" core cannot be used with some
  conurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with
  branch measurement.

  - If the core is not specified and defaults to "sysmon" (Python 3.14+), but
    other settings conflict with sysmon, then the "ctrace" core will be used
    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: if the measurement core defaults to "sysmon" (the default for Python
  3.14+ since v7.9.1), but sysmon can't support some aspect of your
  configuration (concurrency settings, dynamic contexts, and so on), then the
  ctrace core is used instead. Previously, this would result in an error.
  An explicit request
  for sysmon with conflicting settings will still result in an error. Closes
  `issue 2064`_.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

  - Complete parameter reference (16 params with types, ranges, defaults)
  - Response format variants (3 types)
  - Troubleshooting (Opus subscription required, token limits, decoding)
- Updated environment variable defaults: `NOVELAI_MAX_LENGTH=150`, `NOVELAI_MODEL=erato`

```javascript
{
  "input": "プロンプト",
  "model": "erato",

}

author: copilot
body:
Performance analysis identified redundant file operations, complex error handling patterns, and a lambda closure bug causing incorrect delete behavior.

### File I/O Optimization
- Removed redundant `os.path.exists()` checks—exception handling covers all cases
- Replaced `read().strip()` + `json.loads()` with direct `json.load()`
- Consolidated exception blocks: `except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError)`

**Before:**
```python
if os.path.exists(path):
    try:
        with open(path, "r") as f:
            content = f.read().strip()
            if content:
                data = json.loads(content)
            else:
                data = []
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
        data = []
```

**After:**
```python
try:
    with open(path, "r") as f:
        data = json.load(f)
except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
    data = []
```

### Lambda Closure Fix
- Fixed `RiwayatPage` delete buttons capturing wrong index due to late binding
- Changed `lambda index=i` parameter name to `lambda idx=i` to force early binding

body:
Implements the thematic insight extraction agent system specified in the design documents (`Agent-System-Design-Thinking.md` and `Thematic-Insight-Extraction-Agent-System-Architecture.md`).

## Architecture

**4-Stage Pipeline:**
- **Stage 1 (Deconstruction)**: DocumentAnalyzerAgent extracts structured data (principles, rules, tags, evidence)
- **Stage 2 (Categorization)**: ThematicClusteringAgent groups documents via tag-based clustering
- **Stage 3 (Synthesis)**: SynthesisAgent generates insights, identifies contradictions, extracts implications
- **Stage 4 (Validation)**: ValidationAgent scores quality, validates evidence, flags issues

**Pattern Recognition**: FrequencyAnalyzer and CooccurrenceAnalyzer run cross-cutting analysis

**Orchestration**: OrchestratorAgent coordinates workflow with checkpointing after each stage

## Implementation

```python
# Usage
from src.agents import OrchestratorAgent
from src.models import Document

orchestrator = OrchestratorAgent(config)
documents = [Document(id="doc_001", filename="note.md", content="...")]
report = orchestrator.process(documents)  # Returns synthesis with themes, principles, validation
```

**Core Components:**
- 8 agents (`BaseAgent` → specialized agents)
- 6 data models with JSON serialization
- State management with resume capability
- Markdown + JSON output generators

**Key Design Decisions:**
- Mock mode for LLM-free operation (rule-based extraction fallback)
- Immutable state with explicit checkpointing
- Tag-based clustering for MVP (embedding-based clustering deferred to Phase 2)
- Rule-based validation (ML-based deferred to Phase 2)

## Scope

**Included**: Full 4-stage workflow, basic pattern recognition, quality validation, checkpointing, dual output formats

**Deferred**: Enhanced LLM prompts, semantic embeddings, temporal/emotional analyzers, parallel processing, web UI

## Structure

- `src/agents/` - 8 agent implementations (~44 KB)
- `src/models/` - 6 data models (~13 KB)
- `src/utils/` - 5 utilities (config, logging, state, output)
- `examples/basic_example.py` - Demo with in-memory documents
- `data/` - 5 sample documents
- `tests/test_basic.py` - 5 tests covering core functionality

## Display Original Title for Movies and TV Shows

This PR adds automatic display of original titles for movies and TV shows when they differ from the localized version, improving content discoverability and cultural context for international films and series.

### Summary of Changes

* Added `showOriginalTitle` computed property to `MovieInfo.vue` and `TvInfo.vue`
* Display original title as a new field in the stats section when it differs from localized title
* Positioned before "Released" date for movies and "First Aired" for TV shows
* Maintains existing CSS module styling and layout structure

### Motivation

Users frequently need access to original titles for:
- International content where translations differ significantly
- Searching on other platforms using the original name
- Understanding cultural context
- Personal preference for original language titles

TMDB provides `original_title` (movies) and `original_name` (TV shows) which were previously unused in the detail views.

### Implementation Details

**Design Decision**

Initially considered implementing in `Hero.vue` with a toggle button, but the minimalist approach of displaying it directly in `MovieInfo.vue` and `TvInfo.vue` proved cleaner and more consistent with the existing information architecture. The toggle design felt visually intrusive and added unnecessary interaction complexity.

**Conditional Display**

The original title field only appears when it differs from the localized title, avoiding redundant information for content where both are identical (e.g., English films for English-speaking users).

**Component Updates**

Both `MovieInfo.vue` and `TvInfo.vue` received identical implementation:
- Computed property validates title differences
- New list item added to stats section
- Uses existing label/value styling pattern
- No breaking changes to component props or events

### User Experience

**When Original Differs:**
- "Original Title" field appears in stats list
- Displays before release/air date
- Seamlessly integrated with existing information

**When Titles Match:**
- Field is hidden automatically
- No visual clutter or redundancy

### Testing Recommendations

1. Navigate to a foreign film (e.g., Spanish, Japanese, Korean cinema)
2. Verify "Original Title" appears in the info section
3. Check that it displays the non-translated title
4. Navigate to English-language content
5. Confirm the field does not appear
6. Test on both movie and TV show detail pages

### Impact

**User Experience:**
- Improved content discoverability
- Better cultural context for international content
- Cleaner than toggle-based approaches

**Code Quality:**
- Minimal code footprint
- Consistent with existing patterns
- No new dependencies or state management

**Performance:**
- Zero performance impact
- Computed property with simple validation

Closes #89

body:
# Upgrade to Claude Sonnet 4.5 with Extended Thinking Mode

## Summary
This PR replaces the Modal/vLLM inference backend with Claude Sonnet 4.5 through the Anthropic API and implements "extended thinking mode" for better reasoning quality. The changes affect both `main.py` and `backend.py`, updating all LLM calls to use the new API.

**Key changes:**
- Replaced Modal/vLLM endpoint calls with Anthropic API (`claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`)
- Implemented extended thinking at the prompt level by instructing the model to think inside `<thinking>` tags
- Increased `max_tokens` by 800 per request to accommodate thinking tokens
- Updated conversation history structure (removed separate `speaker`/`speaker_name` fields, consolidated to `agent`)
- Added `anthropic==0.72.0` to requirements.txt
- Removed hardcoded API keys (now reads from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable only)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

**⚠️ Risk Level: YELLOW** - Core functionality changed, partial testing completed

- [ ] **Verify API key configuration**: Ensure `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set in your environment. Without it, the system will silently return mock responses instead of failing loudly.

- [ ] **Test full simulation end-to-end**: Run `./run_townhall.sh immigration` with sufficient API credits. My testing ran out of credits after ~12 responses, so full verification is needed. Expected behavior: agents should generate thoughtful, in-character responses about the topic.

- [ ] **Review token budget impact**: Each request now uses `original_max_tokens + 800` tokens (e.g., 1300 instead of 500). Verify this cost increase is acceptable for your use case.

- [ ] **Check extended thinking quality**: Review actual agent responses to confirm the "extended thinking" prompt additions are producing better reasoning. The thinking tags should be stripped from final output (check that `<thinking>...</thinking>` doesn't appear in responses).

- [ ] **Verify conversation history compatibility**: The history structure changed from `speaker`/`speaker_name` to just `agent`. If any downstream code depends on the old structure, it will break.

### Recommended Test Plan
```bash
# 1. Set API key
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key-here"

# 2. Start the server
python main.py

# 3. Run the townhall simulation
./run_townhall.sh immigration

# 4. Verify responses are real (not mock) and coherent
# 5. Check that thinking tags are stripped from output
# 6. Monitor API usage/costs

body:
Integrates OpenStreetMap Nominatim for location search in expense forms, complementing existing GPS and manual entry methods. Uses free, privacy-friendly search without requiring API keys.

**Note**: This PR has been rebased on the latest main branch (7417bc0) for a clean, linear history containing only the place picker feature changes.

## Changes

- **Dependencies**: Added `http: ^1.1.0` for Nominatim API calls

- **Location Input Widget** (`lib/manager/expense/widgets/location/location_input_widget.dart`):
  - Added search button triggering OpenStreetMap search dialog
  - New `_showPlaceSearch()` method handles place selection from Nominatim
  - New `_PlaceSearchDialog` widget with custom OSM integration
  - New `NominatimPlace` model for search results
  - Preserves existing GPS and manual entry flows
  - Integrated with refactored LocationService architecture

- **Localization**: Added `search_place` and `search_place_hint` strings across all 5 languages (IT, EN, ES, PT, ZH)

- **Documentation**: Created `docs/LOCATION_SEARCH.md` with OpenStreetMap implementation details

## Why OpenStreetMap?

- ✅ **Free** - No API key required
- ✅ **Privacy-friendly** - Uses open data from OpenStreetMap
- ✅ **F-Droid compatible** - No proprietary services
- ✅ **Consistent** - Same data source as existing map display
- ✅ **Simple** - Works out of the box with zero configuration

## Implementation Notes

```dart
// Search uses OpenStreetMap's free Nominatim API
Future<void> _showPlaceSearch() async {
  final result = await showDialog<NominatimPlace>(
    context: context,
    builder: (ctx) => _PlaceSearchDialog(hintText: gloc.search_place_hint),
  );
  
  if (result != null) {
    // Nominatim returns coordinates directly
    final location = ExpenseLocation(
      latitude: result.latitude,
      longitude: result.longitude,
      address: result.displayName,
    );
    // Update location with coordinates and address
  }
}
```

Location input now provides three entry methods: search (new, OSM-powered), GPS (existing with LocationService), manual text (existing).

### Nominatim API Usage

- Endpoint: `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/search`
- Rate limit: 1 request per second (500ms debounce implemented)
- User-Agent: `Caravella-ExpenseTracker/1.1.0`
- Complies with OSM usage policy

## Rebase Details

Successfully rebased onto latest main branch (7417bc0) for a clean history:
- **Before**: 4 commits including merge with 52 files changed
- **After**: 2 commits with only 4 files changed (feature-specific changes only)
  - `6f6c18a` - Initial plan
  - `179221a` - OpenStreetMap Nominatim integration
- Location widget integrated with new LocationService architecture from main
- Added `_isResolvingAddress` state variable for search loading states
- Updated to use LocationWidgetConstants for icon consistency

**Note**: Force-push required to update the remote branch due to history rewrite.

## Post-Integration Required

```bash
flutter pub get      # Fetch http dependency
flutter gen-l10n     # Generate translations
flutter analyze      # Verify
flutter test         # Validate no regressions
```

No API key configuration needed - works immediately after build!

> [!NOTE]
> This implementation uses OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service instead of Google Places, providing a free, privacy-friendly, and F-Droid compatible solution. The code has been rebased on the latest main branch and integrated with the refactored LocationService architecture.

- Fixes calca/caravella#279

author: borisquanli
body:
## Executive Summary
Complete modularization of S&P 500 financial analytics Flask backend, establishing enterprise-grade architecture patterns for scalable financial data processing. This refactoring creates the foundation for high-performance FastAPI services while maintaining existing PostgreSQL data pipeline integration.

## Enterprise Technology Alignment
- **Modular Architecture**: Blueprint-based route separation enabling independent service scaling
- **Risk Management**: Comprehensive test coverage with database mocking for safe deployment
- **Data Integrity**: Repository pattern implementation ensuring consistent financial data access
- **Performance Foundation**: Clean separation preparing for FastAPI async processing of market data

## Technical Achievements
✅ **Enterprise Patterns**: Implemented separation of concerns (routes/models/queries)
✅ **Testing Infrastructure**: Production-grade pytest framework with comprehensive mocking
✅ **Database Abstraction**: Repository pattern for scalable financial data operations  
✅ **Docker Ready**: Container-based deployment for enterprise environments

## Technology Stack Integration
This refactoring supports modern financial technology stacks including:

- **Graph Database Ready**: Clean data models prepared for Neo4j relationship mapping
- **FastAPI Foundation**: Modular structure enabling parallel FastAPI development
- **Enterprise Integration**: Architecture patterns supporting Java Spring Boot interoperability
- **Cloud Scale**: Performance and reliability patterns for enterprise deployment

## Next Phase: FastAPI Development
Foundation established for developing high-performance FastAPI services in the same backend package, leveraging the same PostgreSQL data warehouse while providing:
- Async processing for real-time market data
- Automatic OpenAPI documentation
- Enhanced performance for graph database integration
- Modern API patterns for AI/LLM consumption

## Real-World Integration Value
**Production Validation**: This foundational project has been successfully integrated into the OpenBB Platform (Linux Foundation FINOS member) via active contribution ([PR #7264](https://github.com/OpenBB-finance/OpenBB/pull/7264)), demonstrating enterprise-grade Flask-to-FastAPI migration patterns for financial services platforms.

Ready for production deployment and FastAPI parallel development.

    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: if the measurement core defaults to "sysmon" (the default for Python
  3.14+ since v7.9.1), but sysmon can't support some aspect of your
  configuration (concurrency settings, dynamic contexts, and so on), then the
  ctrace core is used instead. Previously, this would result in an error.
  An explicit request
  for sysmon with conflicting settings will still result in an error. Closes
  `issue 2064`_.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

SharedPreferences caching with 24h benchmark validity, per-task/device-profile storage

As per the issue here: https://github.com/ch-robinson/dotnet-avro/issues/314

Please don't hesitate with critical feedback! Surely not the only ones, but a few things worth thinking about:
1. The new additions are all implemented with internal visibility - is that desirable to maintain full flexibility, or should they be public like most (all?) the rest of the library?
2. A static method for recursion seemed easiest here, but do shout if you'd prefer some instance/interface based approach (especially if it was to be exposed public rather than internal)
3. The recursion search effectively assumes reference equality of equal schemas. I think this is done elsewhere too (eg when storing expressions in the recursive case), but just flagging in case you can think of any cases where that would legitimately cause issues

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [pytest](https://pypi.org/project/pytest) from **6.2.1** to **9.0.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 9.0.0
   ```
   =========================

New features
------------


- `1367 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/1367>`_: **Support for subtests** has been added.

  :ref:`subtests <subtests>` are an alternative to parametrization, useful in situations where the parametrization values are not all known at collection time.

  Example:

  .. code-block:: python

      def contains_docstring(p: Path) -> bool:
          """Return True if the given Python file contains a top-level docstring."""
          ...


      def test_py_files_contain_docstring(subtests: pytest.Subtests) -> None:
          for path in Path.cwd().glob("*.py"):
              with subtests.test(path=str(path)):
                  assert contains_docstring(path)


  Each assert failure or error is caught by the context manager and reported individually, giving a clear picture of all files that are missing a docstring.

  In addition, :meth:`unittest.TestCase.subTest` is now also supported.

  This feature was originally implemented as a separate plugin in `pytest-subtests <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-subtests>`__, but since then has been merged into the core.

  .. note::

      This feature is experimental and will likely evolve in future releases. By that we mean that we might change how subtests are reported on failure, but the functionality and how to use it are stable.


- `13743 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13743>`_: Added support for **native TOML configuration files**.

  While pytest, since version 6, supports configuration in ``pyproject.toml`` files under ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]``,
  it does so in an "INI compatibility mode", where all configuration values are treated as strings or list of strings.
  Now, pytest supports the native TOML data model.

  In ``pyproject.toml``, the native TOML configuration is under the ``[tool.pytest]`` table.

  .. code-block:: toml

       pyproject.toml
      [tool.pytest]
      minversion = "9.0"
      addopts = ["-ra", "-q"]
      testpaths = [
          "tests",
          "integration",
      ]

  The ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` table remains supported, but both tables cannot be used at the same time.

  If you prefer to use a separate configuration file, or don't use ``pyproject.toml``, you can use ``pytest.toml`` or ``.pytest.toml``:

  .. code-block:: toml

       pytest.toml or .pytest.toml
      [pytest]
      minversion = "9.0"
      addopts = ["-ra", "-q"]
      testpaths = [
          "tests",
          "integration",
      ]

  The documentation now (sometimes) shows configuration snippets in both TOML and INI formats, in a tabbed interface.

  See :ref:`config file formats` for full details.


- `13823 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13823>`_: Added a **"strict mode"** enabled by the :confval:`strict` configuration option.

  When set to ``true``, the :confval:`strict` option currently enables

  * :confval:`strict_config`
  * :confval:`strict_markers`
  * :confval:`strict_parametrization_ids`
  * :confval:`strict_xfail`

  The individual strictness options can be explicitly set to override the global :confval:`strict` setting.

  The previously-deprecated ``--strict`` command-line flag now enables strict mode.

  If pytest adds new strictness options in the future, they will also be enabled in strict mode.
  Therefore, you should only enable strict mode if you use a pinned/locked version of pytest,
  or if you want to proactively adopt new strictness options as they are added.

  See :ref:`strict mode` for more details.


- `13737 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13737>`_: Added the :confval:`strict_parametrization_ids` configuration option.

  When set, pytest emits an error if it detects non-unique parameter set IDs,
  rather than automatically making the IDs unique by adding `0`, `1`, ... to them.
  This can be particularly useful for catching unintended duplicates.


- `13072 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13072>`_: Added support for displaying test session **progress in the terminal tab** using the `OSC 9;4; <https://conemu.github.io/en/AnsiEscapeCodes.html#ConEmu_specific_OSC>`_ ANSI sequence.
  When pytest runs in a supported terminal emulator like ConEmu, Gnome Terminal, Ptyxis, Windows Terminal, Kitty or Ghostty,
  you'll see the progress in the terminal tab or window,
  allowing you to monitor pytest's progress at a glance.

  This feature is automatically enabled when running in a TTY. It is implemented as an internal plugin. If needed, it can be disabled as follows:
  - On a user level, using ``-p no:terminalprogress`` on the command line or via an environment variable ``PYTEST_ADDOPTS='-p no:terminalprogress'``.
  - On a project configuration level, using ``addopts = "-p no:terminalprogress"``.


- `478 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/478>`_: Support PEP420 (implicit namespace packages) as `--pyargs` target when :confval:`consider_namespace_packages` is `true` in the config.

  Previously, this option only impacted package imports, now it also impacts tests discovery.


- `13678 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13678>`_: Added a new :confval:`faulthandler_exit_on_timeout` configuration option set to "false" by default to let `faulthandler` interrupt the `pytest` process after a timeout in case of deadlock.

  Previously, a `faulthandler` timeout would only dump the traceback of all threads to stderr, but would not interrupt the `pytest` process.

  -- by :user:`ogrisel`.


- `13829 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13829>`_: Added support for configuration option aliases via the ``aliases`` parameter in :meth:`Parser.addini() <pytest.Parser.addini>`.

  Plugins can now register alternative names for configuration options,
  allowing for more flexibility in configuration naming and supporting backward compatibility when renaming options.
  The canonical name always takes precedence if both the canonical name and an alias are specified in the configuration file.



Improvements in existing functionality
--------------------------------------

- `13330 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13330>`_: Having pytest configuration spread over more than one file (for example having both a ``pytest.ini`` file and ``pyproject.toml`` with a ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` table) will now print a warning to make it clearer to the user that only one of them is actually used.

  -- by :user:`sgaist`


- `13574 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13574>`_: The single argument ``--version`` no longer loads the entire plugin infrastructure, making it faster and more reliable when displaying only the pytest version.

  Passing ``--version`` twice (e.g., ``pytest --version --version``) retains the original behavior, showing both the pytest version and plugin information.

  .. note::

      Since ``--version`` is now processed early, it only takes effect when passed directly via the command line. It will not work if set through other mechanisms, such as :envvar:`PYTEST_ADDOPTS` or :confval:`addopts`.


- `13823 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13823>`_: Added :confval:`strict_xfail` as an alias to the ``xfail_strict`` option,
  :confval:`strict_config` as an alias to the ``--strict-config`` flag,
  and :confval:`strict_markers` as an alias to the ``--strict-markers`` flag.
  This makes all strictness options consistently have configuration options with the prefix ``strict_``.

- `13700 <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/13700>`_: `--junitx

body:
Merges fixes from https://github.com/JjyKsi/bmw-cardata-ha/pull/108 addressing GPS desync, missing unit conversions, and MQTT reconnection loops causing HA unresponsiveness.

## Device Tracker (`device_tracker.py`)
- **Hybrid coordinate pairing**: Pairs lat/lon updates within 3s as real-time, accepts delayed pairs (≤180s) if both changed, interpolates single-coordinate updates
- **State restoration**: Restores last known location on restart via `RestoreEntity`
- **Descriptor cleanup**: Removed trip segment GPS descriptors, only tracks `navigation.currentLocation.*`

```python
# Prevents map jumps from lat arriving at 12:00:00, lon at 12:00:45
time_diff = abs(lat_time - lon_time)
if time_diff <= self._short_delay:
    self._apply_new_coordinates(lat, lon, "real-time pair")
elif only_one_differs:
    interp_lon = (lon + self._restored_lon) / 2  # Interpolate older coordinate
```

## Sensor (`sensor.py`)
- **Device class mapping**: Auto-maps 10 unit types (pressure, temperature, voltage, etc.) to HA device classes enabling unit conversion
- **Legacy unit normalization**: Maps `l→L`, `celsius→°C`, `kPa`, `weeks`, `months` to HA standard units
- **Battery sensors**: Removed fixed `mdi:battery-clock` icons; HA now shows charge level in icon

## MQTT Stream (`stream.py`)
- **Circuit breaker**: Blocks reconnections for 5 min after 10 failures in 60s window
- **Connection state tracking**: `ConnectionState` enum distinguishes intentional vs error disconnects
- **Intentional disconnect flag**: Prevents reconnect callbacks during shutdown

Fixes #98, #93, #42, #91

<issue_description># GitHub Copilot Instructions: Agentic Job Hunting Extension

## Project Overview

**Name:** Agentic Job Hunting (AJH)  
**Type:** Chrome Extension (Manifest V3)  
**Purpose:** AI-powered job application form filling assistant using Anthropic's Claude API  
**Architecture:** Hybrid React (popup UI) + Vanilla JavaScript (content scripts, background)  
**Author:** Experienced engineering leader with 15+ years in mobile/cloud/AI

### Mission Statement
Build a reliable, cost-transparent browser extension that intelligently automates job application form filling while maintaining complete user control, privacy, and detailed cost tracking.

---

## Core Principles

When assisting with this project, always consider these principles:

### 1. Cost Consciousness
- **Every API call costs money** - Be judicious with Claude API usage
- Track token consumption for all API interactions
- Show estimated costs BEFORE operations
- Provide optimization suggestions
- Cache responses where appropriate
- User should never be surprised by costs

### 2. User Control & Privacy
- **User approves everything** - No auto-submission, always preview
- All data stored locally (Chrome storage)
- API key encrypted by Chrome
- Only send to Claude API when user explicitly triggers analysis
- Clear data ownership and deletion options

### 3. Reliability & Error Handling
- Graceful degradation when things fail
- Clear, actionable error messages
- Never lose user data (form fills, configuration)
- Handle edge cases (multi-page forms, dynamic fields, etc.)
- Comprehensive validation

### 4. State Management Philosophy
- **Global State:** Reusable settings (API key, resume, profile, standard answers)
- **Application State:** Per-job data (custom resume, cover letter, filled forms, notes)
- Clear separation prevents data loss and enables efficient reuse
- Each application is independent and archivable

---

## Tech Stack

### Core Technologies
- **Manifest V3** - Modern Chrome extension API
- **React 18** - Popup UI only
- **Vanilla JavaScript** - Content scripts, background service worker
- **Chrome Storage API** - Sync for config, Local for application data
- **Anthropic Claude API** - AI form filling engine (Sonnet 4.5)

### Why Hybrid Architecture?
- **React for Popup:** Complex UI with state management, form handling
- **Vanilla JS for Content:** Performance, bundle size, direct DOM manipulation
- **Separation of Concerns:** UI vs. functionality

### Build Tools
- Webpack or Vite for bundling
- Babel for JSX transformation
- ESLint for code quality
- No TypeScript (yet) - may add later

---

## Project Structure

```
ajh-extension/
├── manifest.json              # Extension manifest (V3)
├── src/
│   ├── popup/                 # React popup UI
│   │   ├── App.jsx           # Main popup component
│   │   ├── components/       # UI components
│   │   ├── hooks/            # Custom React hooks
│   │   └── popup.html        # Popup entry point
│   ├── content/              # Content scripts (Vanilla JS)
│   │   ├── formDetector.js   # Detect and analyze forms
│   │   ├── formFiller.js     # Apply fills to forms
│   │   └── pageAnalyzer.js   # Extract job posting info
│   ├── background/           # Service worker (Vanilla JS)
│   │   ├── background.js     # Main service worker
│   │   ├── apiClient.js      # Claude API wrapper
│   │   └── stateManager.js   # Application state handler
│   ├── shared/               # Shared utilities
│   │   ├── storage.js        # Chrome storage wrappers
│   │   ├── constants.js      # App constants
│   │   ├── validation.js     # Input validation
│   │   └── costCalculator.js # Token/cost estimation
│   └── icons/                # Extension icons
├── docs/                     # Documentation

body:
### What is in this PR

This PR introduces the `SlackWriteMessageServiceType` and the `SlackWriteMessageActionNode`. This allows users to send messages to a chosen Slack channel.

We make use of Slack's [Bot token](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/tokens/) authentication:

> Bot tokens represent a bot associated with an app installed in a workspace. Unlike user tokens, they're not tied to a user's identity—they're only tied to your app. Since acting independently allows your app to stay installed even when an installing user is deactivated, using bot tokens is usually for the best.

We could easily add other authentication types in the future.

### How to test this PR

- Add a new "Slack write message" automation node.

author: pionex
body:
When using an Expansion Pin as a User Input, M66 always read 0.  This fix changes the pin type in the UserInput class to InputPin and uses the get() method.  M66 now appears to work.  

I have not yet regression tested to see how this affects non expansion inputs.  I just wanted to post this in case it helps someone with a better understanding of the input classes.  There is an issue where UserInput creates a std::array of the pins, but InputPin requires the pin name to be provided in the ctor.  It would require a number of changes to make this work (array of InputPin* maybe), so right now this just puts a generic pin name / legend so the array can be created during class initialization.

author: mantzas
body:
## Summary

Implement a hybrid Docker registry strategy to avoid Docker Hub rate limits by migrating 5 out of 8 services (62.5%) to alternative registries with no rate limits. Additionally, configure CI/CD with Docker Hub authentication to increase rate limits for the remaining 3 services.

## Changes

### Registry Migration
- **AWS ECR Public (4 services)**: RabbitMQ, MySQL, MongoDB, LocalStack - no rate limits
- **GitHub Container Registry (1 service)**: OpenTelemetry - no rate limits  
- **Docker Hub (3 services)**: Kafka, Valkey, HiveMQ - only available on Docker Hub

### CI/CD Authentication
- **GitHub Actions configured** with Docker Hub login (increases limit from 100 to 200 pulls/6h)
- **Graceful fallback** if secrets are not configured (`continue-on-error: true`)
- **Comprehensive setup guide** for configuring repository secrets

### Files Added
- `docker-compose.hub.yml` - Pure Docker Hub fallback configuration
- `script/docker-registry-helper.sh` - Helper script for configuration management
- `docs/DOCKER_REGISTRY_MIGRATION.md` - Comprehensive migration guide
- `docs/DOCKER_REGISTRY_QUICK_START.md` - Quick reference guide
- `docs/DOCKER_HUB_CI_SETUP.md` - CI setup guide for Docker Hub authentication

### Files Modified
- `docker-compose.yml` - Now uses hybrid registry approach by default
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` - Added Docker Hub authentication to integration-tests and e2e-tests jobs

## Benefits

- **Reduced rate limits**: Only 3/8 services (37.5%) subject to Docker Hub limits
- **CI/CD optimized**: Authentication doubles rate limit (100 → 200 pulls/6h) for remaining services
- **Improved reliability**: Multi-registry redundancy
- **Better performance**: AWS ECR and GHCR often provide faster pulls
- **Zero workflow changes**: Fully backward compatible, no user action required
- **Easy management**: Helper script for status checks and configuration switching

## Testing

- ✅ Validated all docker-compose configurations
- ✅ Tested helper script functionality  
- ✅ Verified images exist on alternative registries
- ✅ Confirmed backward compatibility with Docker Hub fallback
- ✅ Verified CI workflow syntax

## Setup Required (for CI/CD)

To enable Docker Hub authentication in CI and increase rate limits to 200 pulls/6h:

1. Create a Docker Hub access token (read-only permission is sufficient)
2. Add repository secrets:
   - `DOCKERHUB_USERNAME` - Your Docker Hub username
   - `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` - Your Docker Hub access token

📖 **Detailed instructions**: See [`docs/DOCKER_HUB_CI_SETUP.md`](docs/DOCKER_HUB_CI_SETUP.md)

**Note**: CI will work without these secrets (using unauthenticated pulls), but with lower rate limits.

## Migration Impact

### For Developers
```bash
# No changes needed - existing commands work
docker-compose up -d
task deps-start

# Optional: Login for better rate limits
docker login
# or
./script/docker-registry-helper.sh login
```

### For CI/CD
- Rate limit issues reduced by ~62.5% (5/8 services use unlimited registries)
- With Docker Hub authentication: remaining 3 services get 200 pulls/6h (vs 100 unauthenticated)
- Graceful degradation if secrets not configured
- Helper script available for status monitoring

## Documentation

- **Migration guide**: [`docs/DOCKER_REGISTRY_MIGRATION.md`](docs/DOCKER_REGISTRY_MIGRATION.md) - Comprehensive guide with troubleshooting
- **Quick start**: [`docs/DOCKER_REGISTRY_QUICK_START.md`](docs/DOCKER_REGISTRY_QUICK_START.md) - Quick reference
- **CI setup**: [`docs/DOCKER_HUB_CI_SETUP.md`](docs/DOCKER_HUB_CI_SETUP.md) - GitHub Actions secrets setup
- **Helper script**: `./script/docker-registry-helper.sh --help` - Inline help

## Rollback Plan

If issues arise, use the Docker Hub fallback:
```bash
docker-compose -f docker-compose.hub.yml up -d
```

## Changes provided by this PR

This PR optimizes the Dependabot configuration in `.github/dependabot.yml` to improve scheduling and increase the number of allowed concurrent pull requests.

### Problem

Running Dependabot using the monthly schedule results in running the job on the first day of every month. This generates a high load on GitHub systems and causes noticeable delays in running workflows. Additionally, the default limit of 5 open pull requests is often too small, resulting in failing updates due to delayed required updates for some packages.

### Solution

This PR makes the following changes to address these issues:

1. **Randomized Monthly Schedule**: Converts monthly schedules from `interval: monthly` to `interval: cron` with a randomized execution time. The job will now run once a month on a random day (between the 2nd and 28th) at a random time (between 1:00 and 4:00), spreading the load across GitHub systems.

2. **Increased Pull Request Limit**: Sets the `open-pull-requests-limit` to a minimum of 15 (up from the default of 5). This ensures that more dependency updates can be processed simultaneously without blocking critical updates.

3. **Timezone Configuration**: Ensures all schedules use `timezone: Europe/Berlin` for consistent timing.

4. **Multi-directory Support**: If multiple `package.json` files are detected in the repository, the configuration for npm packages is updated to use `directories: "**/*"` instead of `directory: "/"` to properly scan all subdirectories.

### Benefits

- Reduced load on GitHub infrastructure by distributing Dependabot runs across the month
- Faster workflow execution due to reduced system congestion
- More dependency updates can be processed in parallel
- Better handling of repositories with multiple package locations

### Reference

For more information about Dependabot configuration options, see the [GitHub Dependabot Options Reference](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference).

---

## Deutsche Beschreibung

Diese PR optimiert die Dependabot-Konfiguration in `.github/dependabot.yml`, um die Zeitplanung zu verbessern und die Anzahl der gleichzeitig erlaubten Pull Requests zu erhöhen.

### Problem

Die Ausführung von Dependabot mit monatlichem Zeitplan führt dazu, dass der Job am ersten Tag jedes Monats ausgeführt wird. Dies erzeugt eine hohe Last auf den GitHub-Systemen und verursacht spürbare Verzögerungen bei der Ausführung von Workflows. Zusätzlich ist das Standardlimit von 5 offenen Pull Requests oft zu klein, was zu fehlgeschlagenen Updates führt, da erforderliche Aktualisierungen für einige Pakete verzögert werden.

### Lösung

Diese PR führt die folgenden Änderungen durch, um diese Probleme zu beheben:

1. **Randomisierter monatlicher Zeitplan**: Die monatlichen Zeitpläne werden von `interval: monthly` auf `interval: cron` mit einer zufälligen Ausführungszeit umgestellt. Der Job wird nun einmal im Monat an einem zufälligen Tag (zwischen dem 2. und 28.) zu einer zufälligen Uhrzeit (zwischen 1:00 und 4:00 Uhr) ausgeführt, wodurch die Last auf die GitHub-Systeme verteilt wird.

2. **Erhöhtes Pull-Request-Limit**: Das `open-pull-requests-limit` wird auf mindestens 15 gesetzt (statt dem Standard von 5). Dies stellt sicher, dass mehr Abhängigkeits-Updates gleichzeitig verarbeitet werden können, ohne kritische Updates zu blockieren.

3. **Zeitzonenkonfiguration**: Alle Zeitpläne verwenden `timezone: Europe/Berlin` für eine konsistente Zeitplanung.

4. **Unterstützung mehrerer Verzeichnisse**: Wenn mehrere `package.json`-Dateien im Repository erkannt werden, wird die Konfiguration für npm-Pakete aktualisiert, um `directories: "**/*"` anstelle von `directory: "/"` zu verwenden, damit alle Unterverzeichnisse ordnungsgemäß gescannt werden.

### Vorteile

- Reduzierte Last auf die GitHub-Infrastruktur durch Verteilung der Dependabot-Läufe über den Monat
- Schnellere Workflow-Ausführung aufgrund reduzierter Systemauslastung
- Mehr Abhängigkeits-Updates können parallel verarbeitet werden
- Bessere Handhabung von Repositories mit mehreren Paket-Standorten

### Referenz

Weitere Informationen zu den Dependabot-Konfigurationsoptionen finden sich in der [GitHub Dependabot Options Reference](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/dependabot-options-reference).

This commit transforms the journal highlighting system to use TipTap's native Mark system, embedding highlights directly in the document structure. This eliminates offset calculations entirely and provides perfect position accuracy.

## Frontend Changes

### Core Extensions
- Add HighlightMark extension (src/features/journal/extensions/HighlightMark.ts)
  - TipTap Mark extension for highlights embedded in document
  - Stores highlight metadata in mark attributes (id, color, author, etc.)
  - Commands: setHighlight, unsetHighlight, updateHighlightCommentCount
  - Click event handling for highlight interactions

- Add HighlightToolbar component (src/features/journal/components/HighlightToolbar.tsx)
  - Floating toolbar appearing on text selection
  - Color picker with 6 highlight colors
  - Integrates with auth system for author tracking
  - Position-aware rendering above selection

### Editor Integration
- Update extensions.ts to include HighlightMark
- Update RichTextEditor.tsx to support highlight toolbar
- Add enableHighlights and onHighlightCreate props
- Handle highlight-clicked custom events

### Real-Time Sync
- Add useTipTapSync hook (src/features/journal/hooks/useTipTapSync.ts)
  - Real-time document synchronization
  - Broadcast highlight creation/deletion
  - Handle comment count updates
  - WebSocket message handling

## Backend Changes

### Data Models
- Update highlight.py with TipTap-specific models
  - TipTapHighlight model for extracted highlights
  - extract_highlights_from_tiptap() function
  - update_highlight_comment_count_in_tiptap() function
  - remove_highlight_from_tiptap() function

- Update journal.py to support TipTap JSON
  - Add content_tiptap field (Optional[Dict[str, Any]])
  - Maintain content (markdown) for backward compatibility
  - Updated all journal models (Base, Create, Update, Response)

### API Endpoints
- Add tiptap_journals.py routes
  - PUT /api/tiptap/spaces/{space_id}/journals/{journal_id}
    - Update journal with TipTap content
    - Extract and index highlights
    - Broadcast via WebSocket
  - POST /api/tiptap/.../highlights/{highlight_id}/comments/sync
    - Sync comment count to document
  - DELETE /api/tiptap/.../highlights/{highlight_id}
    - Remove highlight from document

### Migration
- Add migrate_highlights_to_tiptap.py script
  - Convert offset-based highlights to TipTap marks
  - Markdown to TipTap JSON conversion
  - Preserve all highlight metadata
  - Dry-run mode for testing
  - Space-specific migration support

## Testing & Documentation

### Tests
- Add TipTapHighlights.test.tsx
  - Test highlight creation with correct attributes
  - Test persistence through save/load cycle
  - Test overlapping highlights
  - Test comment count updates
  - Test highlight removal
  - Performance test with 100+ highlights

### Documentation
- Add tiptap-highlighting-system.md
  - Architecture overview
  - Component descriptions
  - How it works (creation, persistence, sync)
  - Benefits over offset-based system
  - Migration guide
  - Performance benchmarks
  - Troubleshooting guide

## Benefits

✅ Perfect Position Accuracy
- Highlights move with text as content is edited
- No drift when content above is modified
- Works across all document structures

✅ Simplified Architecture
- No offset recalculations needed
- Document is single source of truth
- Simpler real-time synchronization

✅ Better Performance
- < 50ms render time for 100+ highlights
- ~80% less memory per highlight
- No complex position tracking

✅ Handles Complex Cases
- Overlapping highlights
- Multi-paragraph highlights
- Nested structures (lists, tables)
- Real-time collaboration

## Migration Path

Existing offset-based highlights can be migrated using:
```
python -m app.migrations.migrate_highlights_to_tiptap --dry-run
```

## Breaking Changes

None - system is backward compatible. Both offset-based and TipTap-native highlights can coexist during migration period.

        self.pb_peak = QProgressBar()

When a barcode is scanned, redirects to price comparator with pre-filled EAN code. ## Changes ### Camera Capture (`src/scanner.js`) - Integrated `@zxing/library` for real-time barcode detection (EAN-8/13, UPC-A/E) - `getUserMedia` API with `facingMode: 'environment'` for back camera preference - Continuous video stream scanning with validation (8-14 digit codes) - Error handling for permission denial, missing camera, unsupported browsers - **Debouncing**: Prevents duplicate detections within 2 seconds for better performance - **Haptic feedback**: Vibration on successful scan (mobile devices) - **Audio feedback**: Subtle beep sound on barcode detection - **Torch/Flashlight support**: Automatic detection and toggle button for low-light scanning - **Zoom capability**: Programmatic zoom support (1x-3x) for small/distant barcodes - **Scan history**: LocalStorage integration saves last 10 scanned codes with timestamps - **Recent scans display**: Visual list showing scan history with relative timestamps - **Copy to clipboard**: One-click copy function with modern Clipboard API and fallback - **Share functionality**: Web Share API integration with URL fallback for sharing codes ### UI Enhancements (`scanner.html`) - Scan overlay with animated guide line - Status messaging (info/error/success states) - Fallback image upload decodes via same library - Mobile-responsive controls - **Torch button**: Appears when camera is active and device supports flashlight (positioned in video overlay) - **Manual EAN input**: Collapsible section to type codes manually with validation - **Recent scans section**: Displays last 10 scans with timestamps, copy, and share buttons - **Clear history button**: Option to wipe scan history with confirmation - **Accessibility**: ARIA live regions for screen reader support ### Integration (`comparateur-fetch.js`) - URL parameter parsing: `?ean=3017620422003` auto-fills search and triggers fetch - Enables seamless scanner → comparator flow ## Example Usage ```javascript // When barcode detected: handleBarcodeDetected(result) { const barcode = result.getText(); if (!/^\d{8,14}$/.test(barcode)) return; // Save to history saveToRecentScans(barcode); // Provide feedback if (navigator.vibrate) navigator.vibrate(200); playBeep(); window.location.href = `/comparateur.html?ean=${encodeURIComponent(barcode)}`; } // Manual input: handleManualSubmit() { const ean = manualEanInput.value.trim(); if (!/^\d{8,14}$/.test(ean)) { showStatus('Code EAN invalide', 'error'); return; } saveToRecentScans(ean); window.location.href = `/comparateur.html?ean=${ean}`; } // Copy to clipboard: async function copyToClipboard(ean) { if (navigator.clipboard) { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(ean); } else { // Fallback for older browsers const textArea = document.createElement('textarea'); textArea.value = ean; document.body.appendChild(textArea); textArea.select(); document.execCommand('copy'); document.body.removeChild(textArea); } showStatus(`✓ Code ${ean} copié`, 'success'); } ``` ## Screenshots **Scanner Interface with Manual Input** **Manual Input Active** **Recent Scans History with Copy/Share** **Copy Success Feedback** **Auto-redirect to Comparator** --- **Features Added:** - ⚡ Performance optimization with scan debouncing - 📳 Haptic feedback for tactile confirmation (mobile) - 🔊 Audio beep on successful detection - 💡 Torch/flashlight control for better scanning in low light - ⌨️ Manual EAN input for direct code entry - 📝 Scan history tracking in localStorage (last 10 codes) - 📋 Recent scans list with timestamps and click-to-search - 📤 Share codes via Web Share API or copy shareable link - 📁 Copy EAN codes to clipboard with one click - 🗑️ Clear scan history option - 🔍 Camera zoom support for small barcodes - ♿ Enhanced accessibility with ARIA live regions **Input Methods:** 1. **Camera scanning**: Real-time barcode detection from video stream 2. **Image upload**: Fallback for older browsers or when camera unavailable 3. **Manual input**: Direct keyboard entry with validation and Enter key support **Productivity Features:** - **Quick re-search**: Click any code in history to search again - **Easy sharing**: Share product codes with friends/family via native share or copy link - **Clipboard integration**: Copy codes for use in other apps - **Visual history**: See recent scan activity at a glance Dependencies: `@zxing/library@0.21.3` (no vulnerabilities) Scanner code-barres : capture caméra, intégration librairie EAN, interface mobile -
